title: Kingdom of Morgannwg
capsule: Morgannwg was a medieval Welsh kingdom in southeastern Wales that took shape when Morgan Hen ab Owain (Morgan the Old, d. 974) united the older kingdoms of Gwent and Glywysing around 942; the name 'Morgannwg' (Morgan's land) came into general use by the end of the tenth century. Earlier, his grandfather Hywel ap Rhys (d. 886) of Glywysing had submitted to Alfred the Great's overlordship, and Morgan himself acknowledged the West Saxon kings, attending Athelstan's court in 931. The kingdom's unity fragmented after Morgan's death and it was repeatedly contested by other Welsh dynasties, persisting until the Norman lord Robert Fitzhamon overthrew the last native king, Iestyn ap Gwrgant, around 1091 and established a lordship centred on Cardiff.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Morgannwg's general territory in southeast Wales is reasonably established from medieval Welsh genealogical and ecclesiastical sources; exact boundaries between it and neighbouring Welsh kingdoms fluctuated and are not precisely documented.
